title: Choose a project you can finish

explanation.text: A portfolio is proof that you can build things. One small project that works and is explained well is worth more than five big projects that are half done.

items: Can be finished in a few days or a weekend.
Uses your own files or fake data, never other people's private data.
Can be shown in one minute: a screenshot, a short output, or a few lines of text.

explanation.text: **The one-sentence test.** Can you say it like this? "This program takes **[input]** and gives **[output]** for **[who]**." If you cannot say it in one sentence, the project is too big. Make it smaller.
**Write "done when" first.** Decide how you will know the project is finished before you start. Without it, a project never ends, because you keep adding things.
Cut features, not quality. A small tool that handles bad input well looks better than a big tool that crashes.
**Ideas that fit what you already know**

items: Clean a messy list and write a short report (you built one in the Automation module).
Sort messages into labels with a fake or real AI model (you built one in the AI module).
Summarize monthly spending from a CSV file.
Rename and sort files into folders, with a "dry run" first so nothing is lost.
A study planner that shows days left before each exam.
A quiz maker that reads questions from a JSON file.

explanation.title: Project plan
explanation.text: Fill this in before you write code. Keep it to one page. Change it when you learn something new.
explanation.code:
Project name: [short name]

One sentence: This program takes [input] and gives [output] for [who].

The problem it solves: [why someone would want it]

Input: [what goes in: a file, a list, text]
Output: [what comes out: a file, a report, a message]

Steps:
1. [small step]
2. [small step]
3. [small step]

Done when: [3 things you can check, for example "it cleans the sample file", "it never crashes on bad lines", "the README explains how to run it"]

Not now: [ideas for later, so you do not add them today]

examples.title: Too big, then smaller
examples.code:
Too big: "An app that manages my whole life with AI."
Smaller: "A program that reads my study dates and prints how many days are left for each exam."

examples.title: A weak plan, then a better plan
examples.code:
Weak: "Done when it is good."
Better: "Done when it reads the sample file, prints a report with totals, and shows a clear message if the file is missing."

quiz.question: Which is the better portfolio choice?
options: Five big projects, all half done
One small project that works and is explained
A copy of someone else's project
quiz.explanation: A small finished project is real proof. Half-done work does not show much.

quiz.question: What does the one-sentence test check?
options: If the project is small and clear enough
If the project has a logo
quiz.explanation: If you cannot say what goes in, what comes out and who it helps in one sentence, the project is too big.

quiz.question: Why write "done when" before you start?
options: So you know when to stop
So nobody can see your plan
quiz.explanation: It gives you a finish line, so you do not keep adding features forever.
